about: The interior of the penis: the tunica albuginea, the two corpora cavernosa, the corpus spongiosum with its bulb, the glans, the urethra, the paired deep arteries and dorsal arteries, and the deep dorsal vein. How full the erectile tissue is shows in colour, glow and the speed of the streams; the organ's size and pose are not changed here. The circumflex veins, the fascial layers, the nerves, the corona of the glans and the real cross-sectional shapes are left out, and the sizes are chosen to read clearly rather than measured. Finer structures (marked as children in the Structures list) appear when their parent is selected or the camera is close; they are schematic drawings, and counts, sizes and layout are illustrative, not measured.

GH14.label: Hall JE, Hall ME. Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th ed. Elsevier, 2021.

GRAYS42.label: Standring S (ed). Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice, 42nd ed. Elsevier, 2020.

parts.label: Tunica Albuginea
parts.summary: The tough fibrous sleeve round the erectile tissue of the shaft
parts.function: The tunica albuginea is a dense fibrous sheath round each corpus cavernosum. When the cavernous spaces fill with blood it limits the stretch of the tissue, and the pressure inside rises until the shaft is rigid. It also compresses the small veins that cross it, which restricts the outflow of blood. It is drawn as glass so that the parts inside can be seen.

drives.note: The sleeve is stretched as the erectile tissue fills.

parts.label: Right Corpus Cavernosum
parts.summary: The right of the two main columns of erectile tissue
parts.function: Each corpus cavernosum is a column of spongy tissue made of blood-filled spaces lined by endothelium and separated by smooth muscle. At rest the muscle is contracted and the spaces are small. When the muscle relaxes and the arteries dilate, blood fills the spaces. It deepens in colour and glows more as the tissue fills.

drives.note: The tissue fills with blood as the vasocongestion rises.
Erection is brought about mainly by parasympathetic nerves.

parts.label: Left Corpus Cavernosum
parts.summary: The left of the two main columns of erectile tissue
parts.function: The two corpora cavernosa lie side by side on the upper side of the shaft and are partly separated by a septum. Each begins at the back as a crus attached to the pubic bone. It deepens in colour and glows more as the tissue fills.

drives.note: The tissue fills with blood as the vasocongestion rises.
Erection is brought about mainly by parasympathetic nerves.

parts.label: Corpus Spongiosum
parts.summary: The column of erectile tissue below the corpora that carries the urethra
parts.function: The corpus spongiosum lies on the underside of the shaft. It swells at the back into the bulb and at the front into the glans, and the urethra runs through it. Its tunica is thinner than that of the corpora cavernosa, so it stays softer and keeps the urethra open when the shaft is erect.

drives.note: It fills with blood in erection, though less firmly than the corpora cavernosa.

parts.label: Glans Penis
parts.summary: The cap of erectile tissue at the tip of the penis
parts.function: The glans is the expanded end of the corpus spongiosum and caps the ends of the two corpora cavernosa. The urethra opens at its tip. It is richly supplied with sensory nerve endings. It is drawn as glass so that the urethra inside is visible.

drives.note: The glans fills with blood in erection.

parts.label: Penile Urethra
parts.summary: The urethra within the corpus spongiosum, from the bulb to the tip
parts.function: The penile urethra is the longest part of the male urethra. It begins in the bulb, runs through the corpus spongiosum, and opens at the tip of the glans. It carries urine from the bladder and, at ejaculation, semen. It is drawn as glass.

drives.note: Semen passes along it at ejaculation.

parts.label: Deep (Cavernosal) Arteries
parts.summary: The paired arteries that run down the core of the corpora cavernosa
parts.function: Each corpus cavernosum is supplied by a deep artery that runs along its core and gives off small branches that open into the cavernous spaces. When the smooth muscle relaxes these arteries dilate. In the simulator, the stream in them speeds up and thickens as vasocongestion rises.

drives.note: Inflow rises as the arteries dilate.

parts.label: Dorsal Arteries
parts.summary: The paired arteries on the upper surface of the shaft, supplying the glans
parts.function: Two dorsal arteries run along the upper surface of the shaft, one on each side of the deep dorsal vein, and supply the skin, the glans and the corpus spongiosum. Like the deep arteries they carry more blood as the tissue fills, which is shown by a faster, thicker stream.

drives.note: Inflow rises with the filling of the tissue.

parts.label: Deep Dorsal Vein
parts.summary: The single vein on the upper midline that drains the shaft
parts.function: The deep dorsal vein runs along the midline of the upper surface, between the two dorsal arteries, and drains blood from the glans and the cavernous tissue. As the corpora fill they press the small draining veins against the tunica, so the outflow falls and blood is held in the shaft. In the simulator, its stream thins as vasocongestion rises.

drives.note: Outflow is restricted as the tissue fills and compresses the veins.

parts.label: Crura
parts.summary: The two tapering rear ends of the corpora cavernosa, fixed to the pubic bone
parts.function: Each crus is the back end of a corpus cavernosum. It is attached to the bone of the pelvis and anchors the penis. It is covered by the ischiocavernosus muscle.

drives.note: The erectile tissue fills with blood.

parts.label: Bulb
parts.summary: The expanded back end of the corpus spongiosum
parts.function: The bulb is the widened rear end of the corpus spongiosum, below the crura. The urethra enters it from above. It is covered by the bulbospongiosus muscle.

drives.note: The erectile tissue fills with blood.

parts.label: Bulbospongiosus
parts.summary: The muscle that covers the bulb
parts.function: The bulbospongiosus is a skeletal muscle that surrounds the bulb and the back of the corpus spongiosum. Its rhythmic contractions at orgasm help to expel semen along the urethra.

drives.note: It contracts rhythmically at orgasm.

parts.label: Ischiocavernosus
parts.summary: The muscles that cover the crura
parts.function: Each ischiocavernosus is a skeletal muscle that covers a crus. Its contraction squeezes the crus and helps to maintain the erection.

drives.note: It presses on the crus when the tissue is full.

parts.label: Deep (Buck) Fascia
parts.summary: The strong sheath that surrounds the three erectile columns together
parts.function: Buck fascia is a strong layer of connective tissue that wraps the corpora cavernosa and the corpus spongiosum together. The deep dorsal vein and the dorsal arteries and nerves run beneath it.

parts.label: Suspensory Ligament
parts.summary: A fibrous band that holds the root of the penis to the pubic bone
parts.function: The suspensory ligament is a fibrous band that runs from the front of the pubic bone to the fascia of the penis. It holds the root of the penis in place.

parts.label: Prepuce (Foreskin)
parts.summary: The fold of skin that covers the glans
parts.function: The prepuce is a double fold of skin that covers the glans. In some men it has been removed by circumcision. It is drawn as a loose glass collar behind the glans.

parts.label: Frenulum
parts.summary: The small fold on the underside that joins the glans to the prepuce
parts.function: The frenulum is a small midline fold of skin on the underside of the glans that attaches the prepuce to it.

parts.label: Navicular Fossa
parts.summary: The widened end of the urethra inside the glans
parts.function: The navicular fossa is a short widening of the urethra just before its opening in the glans.

drives.note: Semen passes through it at ejaculation.

parts.label: External Urethral Orifice
parts.summary: The opening of the urethra at the tip of the glans
parts.function: The external urethral orifice is the slit-like opening at the tip of the glans where urine and semen leave the body.

drives.note: Semen leaves the body here.

parts.label: Dorsal Nerves
parts.summary: The paired sensory nerves that run along the upper surface
parts.function: The dorsal nerves of the penis are branches of the pudendal nerve. They run along the upper surface beside the dorsal arteries and carry sensation from the glans and the shaft.

drives.note: Touch signals rise with sexual stimulation.

parts.label: Cavernous Spaces (Right Corpus)
parts.summary: The blood-filled spaces that make up the erectile tissue
parts.function: The cavernous spaces are the small chambers, lined by endothelium, that make up the erectile tissue. When the arteries open they fill with blood and the penis hardens.

drives.note: Blood fills the spaces as the arteries open.

parts.label: Helicine Arteries (Right Corpus)
parts.summary: Coiled branches of the cavernosal artery that open into the spaces
parts.function: The helicine arteries are coiled small arteries that open into the cavernous spaces. They straighten and widen when the muscle in their walls relaxes, and so let blood rush in.

drives.note: The muscle in their walls relaxes during arousal.

parts.label: Trabeculae (Right Corpus)
parts.summary: The strands of smooth muscle and connective tissue between the spaces
parts.function: The trabeculae are strands of smooth muscle and fibrous tissue that form the walls between the cavernous spaces. When the muscle is relaxed the spaces open and fill.

drives.note: The muscle relaxes as the spaces fill.

parts.label: Cavernous Spaces (Left Corpus)
parts.summary: The blood-filled spaces that make up the erectile tissue
parts.function: The cavernous spaces are the small chambers, lined by endothelium, that make up the erectile tissue. When the arteries open they fill with blood and the penis hardens. The same arrangement is drawn in both corpora.

drives.note: Blood fills the spaces as the arteries open.

parts.label: Helicine Arteries (Left Corpus)
parts.summary: Coiled branches of the cavernosal artery that open into the spaces
parts.function: The helicine arteries are coiled small arteries that open into the cavernous spaces. They straighten and widen when the muscle in their walls relaxes, and so let blood rush in.

drives.note: The muscle in their walls relaxes during arousal.

parts.label: Trabeculae (Left Corpus)
parts.summary: The strands of smooth muscle and connective tissue between the spaces
parts.function: The trabeculae are strands of smooth muscle and fibrous tissue that form the walls between the cavernous spaces. When the muscle is relaxed the spaces open and fill.

drives.note: The muscle relaxes as the spaces fill.
